While the [Middle East conflict](https://www.jpmorgan.com/insights/global-research/current-events/iran-conflict-ripple-effects) has sent energy prices soaring, the Federal Reserve (Fed) opted to keep interest rates steady at 3.5–3.75% at its last meeting in March. Generally, the Fed is seen as more likely to cut rates only if the [labor market](https://www.jpmorgan.com/insights/global-research/outlook/labor-market-forecast-2026) weakens significantly or if the economic fallout from higher energy prices becomes more severe. Raising interest rates can help calm inflation, but it can also slow economic growth and increase the already discouraging unemployment rate.
